meta.ogDescription: EQX: Deep-value gold producer at 6.0x PE. Merger de-risked (ISS + Glass Lewis vote FOR), but support broke. Score 72/100.

verdict.summary: Equinox trades at 6.0x forward earnings and 5.98x EV/EBITDA, the cheapest of the North American gold majors, after falling 48% from its 52-week high. The single biggest overhang just lifted: on July 10 both ISS and Glass Lewis told shareholders to vote FOR the all-share Orla merger, which builds a 1.1M oz/year producer with a path to 1.9M oz. Revenue grew 224% on 59% gross margins. What still holds the grade at B+: the chart lost its $10.26 shelf and there is no intact support until $6.46, Q2 output slipped year-over-year, and the deal still dilutes existing holders by roughly a third. This is a contrarian value entry for gold bulls with patience, not a chart you buy for momentum.

business.overview:
Equinox Gold is a mid-tier gold producer headquartered in Vancouver, operating mines across North America (Canada, USA, Mexico). The company produced a record 922,827 ounces in 2025 from a diversified portfolio anchored by the flagship Greenstone Mine in Ontario, Canada's newest large-scale gold mine.

In May 2026, Equinox announced a transformative all-share merger with Orla Mining (1.00 EQX per ORLA share), creating a senior gold producer with 1.1M oz annual production and a funded growth trajectory to 1.9M oz by 2030. The combined entity will have a pure North American footprint after the $1.1B Brazil divestiture in January 2026. The deal, backed by billionaire Pierre Lassonde, is expected to close Q3 2026; as of July 10 both ISS and Glass Lewis had recommended shareholders on each side vote FOR it, clearing the last major hurdle before the vote.

Key assets include Greenstone (550K oz capacity, lowest AISC in portfolio), Los Filos (Mexico, legacy open-pit under optimization), Castle Mountain (Nevada), and post-merger additions of Orla's Camino Rojo and South Railroad projects providing organic growth without construction capex.

business.moat: Scale advantage post-Orla merger (1.1M oz = senior producer status), pure North American jurisdiction (lower geopolitical risk vs Africa/LatAm peers), and Greenstone's low-cost production provide a moderate moat. No pricing power — pure gold price taker.
business.theme: Gold producer consolidation — scale through M&A to attract institutional capital and lower cost of capital, with a multi-year gold bull market as tailwind.

news.title: Proxy Advisors ISS and Glass Lewis Recommend Shareholders Vote FOR the Orla Merger
news.detail: Both independent advisory firms back the share-issuance resolution on the EQX side and the arrangement resolution on the Orla side. Clearest sign yet the deal clears its shareholder vote.

news.title: Equinox Sells Versamet Royalties Stake for C$130M
news.detail: Monetizes a royalty holding for C$130M, adding liquidity ahead of the merger close and trimming non-core exposure.

news.title: Q2 Gold Production Falls Year-Over-Year
news.detail: Quarterly operations update shows Q2 output below the prior year, a reminder that the Brazil divestiture and Greenstone ramp are still reshaping the production base.

news.title: Orla Mining Produces 88,265 Gold Ounces in Q2
news.detail: The merger partner posts its Q2 figures, giving the market a first look at the combined production profile that will define the enlarged company.

news.title: Equinox Gold and Orla Mining Combine to Create a New Senior Gold Producer
news.detail: Landmark all-share merger announced at 1.00 EQX per Orla share. Combined 1.1M oz production, growth path to 1.9M oz, Pierre Lassonde backing.

earnings.beatNote: Three beats in four quarters, then the Q1 2026 miss ($0.23 vs $0.29). The stumble lines up with the Greenstone ramp, Brazil-sale charges and merger costs rather than a demand problem, but a broken beat streak still fails the A+ earnings screen. The next report, due in August, is the first clean read on the combined production base after the Q2 output dip.

insiders.signal: No insider buying or selling flagged in the last 90 days. Institutions hold 67.0%, high for a mid-cap miner and a sign of broad fund and ETF inclusion (EQX is a GDX/GDXJ constituent). Founder-chairman Ross Beaty owns roughly 3.5%, and Pierre Lassonde's backing of the Orla deal adds a well-known name to the register.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: 789.2M shares outstanding today, 759.5M in the float (96.3%). The Orla merger adds roughly 389M new shares, taking the count to about 1,178M and cutting existing holders to near two-thirds of the combined company. With ISS and Glass Lewis backing the vote, the dilution is close to a done deal, and the C$130M Versamet sale gives management extra cash flexibility into the close. No separate ATM or shelf raise surfaced in the filings reviewed.

shortInterest.trend: June 30 FINRA settlement puts short interest around 37M shares, roughly 4.9% of float, days-to-cover near 2.6.
shortInterest.squeezeScore: Low — borrow is effectively free and the stock is not on any most-shorted or high-borrow list. The short position reads as merger arbitrage and gold-beta hedging, not a targeted bear raid.

options.skew: Call-heavy open interest, but day-to-day option volume is thin
options.unusual: Call open interest (69,985 contracts into the July 17 expiry) dwarfs puts (6,539), an OI call/put ratio of 10.7 that leans toward a bounce. Max pain sits at $10.00, a shade above spot, and can act as a pin into expiry. Day-to-day option volume is thin, so treat this as background positioning.

macro.impact: The tape is firmly risk-on (defensiveness score 0.6 out of 100), the worst weather for gold miners: money chases growth and leaves safe havens alone. But the 5-day model puts about 26% odds on a shift toward risk-off, and that rotation is exactly the spark this trade needs. With a 0.69 correlation to gold and a 2.40 beta, EQX lags when equities run and can snap back hard when fear returns. Gold itself, off just 4.6% year-to-date, still leaves the miners with wide margins.

risks.riskSummary: High-beta gold miner in a downtrend, mid-way through an all-share merger that dilutes existing holders by roughly a third. The cheap valuation (6.0x P/E, 5.98x EV/EBITDA) is real, but so is the broken chart, the softer Q2 output, and a risk-on tape that starves miners of flows. The merger-block risk has dropped now that proxy advisors back the vote.

riskCards.title: Orla Merger Dilution
points: All-share deal at 1.00 EQX per Orla share, no cash component
Existing EQX holders diluted to about two-thirds of the combined company
Roughly 389M new shares issued, taking the count from 789M to about 1,178M
ISS and Glass Lewis now recommend voting FOR (Jul 10), so a rejection looks unlikely
Closing still expected Q3 2026, subject to final regulatory sign-off
riskCards.verdict: The dilution is now close to certain but so is the strategic payoff: a 1.1M oz producer with a path to 1.9M oz. With proxy advisors onside, the overhang is more resolved than risky, and a post-close re-rating is the bull case.

performance.alpha: The split personality is the whole story. Over the past year EQX is up 60%, well ahead of GDX (+46%) and GLD (+24%), yet year-to-date it has given back 30% while the miners' ETF lost only 12%. That 18-point YTD gap versus GDX is the merger overhang and the Q1 miss doing their work.

tradeIdea.entryNote: Scale in at spot; broken structure argues for a partial, not a full, position
tradeIdea.thesis: This is a value entry, not a technical one, and the two are pulling in opposite directions. On fundamentals EQX is the cheapest of the majors at 6.0x forward earnings, trades near its $7.76 book value, and just watched its biggest overhang lift as ISS and Glass Lewis backed the Orla merger. On the chart it has lost the $10.26 shelf with nothing structural until $6.46. The way to hold both truths: keep the position partial, use the wide stop the volatility demands, and let the merger close and the enlarged company re-rate. The reward is the gap between a 6x mid-tier and a re-rated senior producer; the risk is that the chart fills its air pocket first.
